$comment: Virtual skill packs — role-based bundles for one-command install. Packs are METADATA ONLY: skills stay in flat skills/<name> folders (golden rule: skills are discovered by path), every skill and every loop belongs to exactly one pack (RFC-0033 — the shape a later physical packs/<name>/ layout needs), and a pack may `requires` the `core` pack, which every installer then installs with it. validate.py enforces all of this. Install a pack with `python3 pack.py <pack> --install`; see README. Rationale: docs/rfcs/0001-skill-packs.md. `outcomes` (RFC-0026) is the second browse axis: packs say WHO needs a skill, outcomes say WHY someone opens the catalogue. It is the README's nine categories restated as seven outcomes and made machine-readable so the site cannot drift from them. Outcomes are a browse aid only — not an install unit — and validate.py enforces the same two-way check packs get.

core.description: The cross-role toolkit every pack builds on: structured intake, document critique, the review council, and output hygiene, plus the ship-a-draft wrapper. Installed automatically with every role pack.

first-value.starter-task: Turn rough notes into a structured brief, then get a verdict on the draft
first-value.starter-prompt: Here are my notes from today's planning call: <paste them>. Turn them into a brief, then critique the draft you write from it.
first-value.verification: brief-intake returns a structured brief with gaps tagged, and doc-critique ends with a verdict: SHIP IT, SHIP WITH CHANGES, MAJOR REWRITE or WRONG ARTIFACT.
first-value.recovery: If neither skill activates, check that `brief-intake/SKILL.md` and `doc-critique/SKILL.md` exist in your skills folder (`~/.claude/skills/` by default). In Claude Code, start a new session after installing.

solution-architect.description: Design-phase artifacts: diagrams, decision records, design docs, contracts, schemas, threat models, and the reviews that gate them.

first-value.starter-task: Record an architecture decision your team already made
first-value.starter-prompt: Write an ADR: we're moving our session store from Redis to DynamoDB. We considered staying on Redis, DynamoDB, and Postgres; we chose DynamoDB for managed scaling and lower ops load.
first-value.verification: adr-generator returns an ADR with context, the options considered with their trade-offs, the decision, and its consequences.
first-value.recovery: If adr-generator does not activate, ask for it by name ("use adr-generator") and check that its folder exists in your skills folder (`~/.claude/skills/` by default).

product-manager.description: Direction to requirements: PR/FAQs, strategy frameworks, OKRs, business cases, interviews, PRDs, journey maps, and success measurement.

first-value.starter-task: Pressure-test a product idea before anyone builds it
first-value.starter-prompt: Write a PR/FAQ for a feature that lets customers pause their subscription for up to three months instead of cancelling.
first-value.verification: prfaq returns a launch press release, a customer FAQ and an internal FAQ that names the hard questions.
first-value.recovery: If prfaq does not activate, ask for it by name ("use prfaq") and check that its folder exists in your skills folder (`~/.claude/skills/` by default).

dev-team.description: Build-and-ship: story splitting, implementation with adversarial review, test plans, triage, migrations, launch readiness, release notes, agent-policy files, and code-quality gates.

prerequisites: A git repository with changes on a branch
The reviewer subagents, for the full panel: `skilldrop install --panel review` (the Claude plugin includes them)
first-value.starter-task: Find out whether your current branch is safe to merge
first-value.starter-prompt: Is this branch safe to merge? Run a pre-merge review on the current diff.
first-value.verification: pre-merge-review runs the project's lint, typecheck and tests through its gate script, then the reviewer panel, and ends with READY or NOT READY.
first-value.recovery: If the gate script cannot find your lint or test commands, tell it what they are. If the panel is skipped, install the reviewer subagents with `skilldrop install --panel review`.

sre-oncall.description: Operate the service: runbooks, observability design, incident communications, postmortems, and capacity/cost models.

first-value.starter-task: Write the runbook an on-call engineer can follow at 3am
first-value.starter-prompt: Write a runbook for our payments-api service: it runs in the Kubernetes namespace payments, depends on Postgres and Stripe, and pages the payments on-call rotation.
first-value.verification: runbook-generator returns a runbook with rollback commands, the common incidents and what to do for each, and an escalation path. Facts you did not give it are marked missing, not invented.
first-value.recovery: If runbook-generator does not activate, ask for it by name ("use runbook-generator") and check that its folder exists in your skills folder (`~/.claude/skills/` by default).

stakeholder-comms.description: Non-technical audiences: audience profiling, deck outlines and real .pptx decks, exec summaries, decision logs, and guides.

first-value.starter-task: Turn a long document into a one-page summary for leadership
first-value.starter-prompt: Turn this design doc into a one-page executive summary for our steering committee: <paste the doc>.
first-value.verification: exec-summary returns a one-page summary that a time-poor reader can act on in 30 seconds, written without jargon.
first-value.recovery: If exec-summary does not activate, ask for it by name ("use exec-summary") and check that its folder exists in your skills folder (`~/.claude/skills/` by default).

ai-engineering.description: Adopt and build AI systems: readiness assessment, use-case triage, rollout and acceptable-use policy, plus agent loop design, subagent orchestration, spend budgets, agent security review, eval harnesses, and AI-usage reporting.

first-value.starter-task: Find out whether a team is ready to adopt AI tools, and what blocks it first
first-value.starter-prompt: Are we ready for AI? Our support team has 12 people on Zendesk, no AI tools today, and a legal team worried about customer data.
first-value.verification: ai-readiness-assessment scores six dimensions (data, tooling, skills, governance, process, culture) with evidence for each, and ranks the gaps that block adoption first.
first-value.recovery: If ai-readiness-assessment does not activate, ask for it by name and check that its folder exists in your skills folder (`~/.claude/skills/` by default).

claude-api.description: Skills for teams building on the Anthropic API — prompt caching, token budgeting, eval generation for skills, and tool-use schema writing.

prerequisites: A system prompt and a typical request from your Claude API integration
first-value.starter-task: Find where prompt caching will cut your input costs
first-value.starter-prompt: Here is our system prompt and a typical request: <paste them>. Where should the cache_control breakpoints go, and what hit rate should we expect?
first-value.verification: prompt-caching-advisor marks where each cache_control checkpoint goes and estimates the cache hit rate.
first-value.recovery: If prompt-caching-advisor does not activate, ask for it by name and check that its folder exists in your skills folder (`~/.claude/skills/` by default).

decide-what-to-build.description: Turn a direction into a committed, measurable plan: press releases, strategy frameworks, OKRs, business cases, requirements, PRDs, and the metrics that will say whether it worked.

design-the-system.description: Commit the shape before the code: decision records, design docs, diagrams, contracts, schemas, migration and threat models, and the design of any agentic parts.

build-and-review-software.description: The loop around the code itself: supervised implementation, adversarial review panels, test plans, triage, accessibility and static-analysis passes, and the policy files agents read.

build-on-the-claude-api.description: Skills for teams building directly on the Anthropic API — prompt caching strategy, token budgeting, eval generation, and tool-use schema writing.

run-and-recover-the-service.description: Operate what shipped: runbooks, observability design, release notes, incident communication, and the postmortem that closes the loop.

explain-it-to-decision-makers.description: Get a non-technical audience to a decision: audience profiling, deck outlines and real decks, exec summaries, decision logs, and how-to guides.

govern-ai-use.description: Adopt AI deliberately and prove what it is doing: readiness assessment, use-case triage, rollout plans, acceptable-use policy, adoption staging, and usage reporting.

get-a-draft-ready-to-ship.description: The passes either side of a generator: collect a messy input into a structured brief, critique the argument, and strip the machine artifacts before it leaves the building.
